subject: psychiatry
title: Intellectual Disability and Autism Spectrum Disorder

steps.tx: **Intellectual disability**, formerly termed mental retardation, is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by significant deficits in both intellectual functioning and adaptive behavior. Diagnostically, deficits must manifest during the developmental period prior to age 18, confirmed by clinical evaluation and individualized standardized psychometric intelligence testing.
steps.say: Intellectual disability features deficits in intellectual and adaptive functioning with onset before age eighteen, verified by clinical and psychometric testing.

left.title: Intellectual Deficits
points: Reasoning, problem solving, and abstract thought
Planning, academic learning, and practical judgement
Standardized IQ score approximately 70 or below
Tested via Wechsler Scales or Binet-Kamat test

right.title: Adaptive Functioning Deficits
points: Practical domain: personal care, money, job safety
Determines level of daily community support needed

steps.tx: **Severity stratification of intellectual disability** divides into four categories: mild (IQ 50 to 69, educable, mental age 9 to 12 years, capable of independent living and unskilled employment), moderate (IQ 35 to 49, trainable, mental age 6 to 9 years), severe (IQ 20 to 34), and profound (IQ under 20).
steps.say: Severity ranges from mild educable disability (IQ 50-69) to moderate trainable, severe, and profound requiring total nursing care.

vis.title: Intellectual Disability Severity Strata
rows: Eighty-five percent of cases; independent living with guidance
Sheltered workshop employment; requires supervised group living
Limited speech; needs daily assistance with all hygiene
Non-verbal; total dependent nursing and medical care

steps.tx: **Etiological classification of intellectual disability** encompasses genetic and environmental causes, where Down syndrome (trisomy 21) is the most common genetic cause overall, and Fragile X syndrome is the most common inherited genetic cause. Fetal alcohol syndrome represents the most common entirely preventable environmental cause worldwide.
steps.say: Down syndrome is the most common genetic cause, Fragile X is the leading inherited cause, and fetal alcohol syndrome is the most common preventable cause.

vis.title: Major Causes of Intellectual Disability
rows: Simian crease, brushfield spots, early Alzheimer disease
Long face, large everted ears, macroorchidism
Happy puppet demeanor, paroxysmal laughter, ataxia

steps.tx: **Autism spectrum disorder**, abbreviated ASD, is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by persistent deficits in social communication and social interaction across multiple contexts, alongside restricted, repetitive patterns of behavior, interests, or activities. Diagnostic features must be present in early development, causing clinically significant functional impairment.
steps.say: Autism spectrum disorder features persistent deficits in social communication combined with restricted, repetitive patterns of behavior and interests.

vis.alt: Autism spectrum disorder core developmental dyads: social-communication deficits and restricted repetitive behaviors
vis.caption: Autism spectrum disorder core developmental dyads: social-communication deficits and restricted repetitive behaviors.

steps.tx: **Joint attention deficits** represent the earliest and most sensitive developmental hallmark of autism spectrum disorder, typically identifiable between nine and 14 months of age. Autistic toddlers fail to point at distant objects to share interest (protodeclarative pointing) or follow a caregiver's gaze to an object.
steps.say: Absence of joint attention by twelve months is an early sign of autism, with failure to point to share interest or follow parental gaze.

left.title: Protodeclarative Pointing (Shared Interest)
points: Points at airplane to say: 'Look at that!'
Monitors adult face to ensure gaze alignment
Intrinsic joy in shared social experience
Severely delayed or absent in autistic toddlers

right.title: Protoimperative Pointing (Demanding)
points: Points at juice cup to say: 'Give me that!'
Treats caregiver as a mechanical tool

steps.tx: **Theory of mind deficit**, or impaired mentalizing capacity, describes the inability of individuals with autism to attribute mental states, including beliefs, desires, and intentions, to others. Demonstrable on Sally-Anne false-belief developmental tasks, autistic children struggle to comprehend that another person can hold beliefs different from reality.
steps.say: Theory of mind impairment prevents autistic children from understanding that others hold different beliefs, as tested by the Sally-Anne false-belief task.

nodes.label: Sally puts marble in basket; Anne moves it to box while Sally is away
Question: 'Where will Sally look for her marble when she returns?'
Normal 4-year-old: 'In the basket' (understands Sally's false belief)
Autistic child: 'In the box' (cannot separate own knowledge from Sally's)

steps.tx: **Applied behavior analysis**, abbreviated ABA, represents the primary evidence-based intensive behavioral intervention for young children with autism spectrum disorder. Initiated before four years of age at 20 to 40 hours weekly, discrete trial training systematically shapes language, eye contact, self-help skills, and peer social play.
steps.say: Applied behavior analysis is the premier early intervention for autism, using discrete trial training to systematically build communication and social skills.

nodes.label: Antecedent: Therapist presents clear verbal command and visual cue
Behavior: Child performs targeted social response or vocalization
Consequence: Immediate positive reinforcement with preferred reward
Inter-trial pause of five seconds before next learning trial

steps.tx: **Pharmacotherapy in autism spectrum disorder** does not treat core social or communication deficits, but targets severe irritability, temper tantrums, physical aggression, and deliberate self-injurious behavior. Risperidone and aripiprazole are the only psychotropics approved by regulatory authorities for managing severe irritability and aggression in ASD.
steps.say: Medications cannot correct core autism deficits, but risperidone and aripiprazole are approved to treat severe aggression and head-banging tantrums.

vis.title: Medications for Comorbid ASD Behaviors
rows: D2/5-HT2A block; monitor prolactin & weight gain
D2 partial agonist; lower metabolic liability
Lower response rate & higher irritability than in pure ADHD
Limited efficacy; high risk of motor activation
